_what_this_is: Delivery profiles for master.py. Each is a loudness target, a true-peak
ceiling, and how much limiting is allowed in service of the target.
Profiles set LOUDNESS ONLY. They deliberately do not carry EQ: tonal moves
stay explicit (--eq), because a profile that quietly reshapes the spectrum
is a profile nobody can reason about.
These two exist because the same master does not win everywhere. Verified
by listening on this project's own material: the louder, limited version
sounded better on a real bass system and worse on laptop and work speakers.
That is the normal split -- on a big rig, limiting reads as density and
power; on a small driver there is no sub to carry it and the same limiting

device.summary: Laptops, phones, desktop and work speakers. The default.
rationale: Sits where the blend already lands, so the limiter never engages and the
master costs nothing in transients -- it is a safety pass: per-track
level match, peak ceiling, mono check.
Measured on this material: 0% limiting, loudness range unchanged at
2.9 LU, short-term crest held at 9.20 dB.

club.summary: PA and sub-equipped systems, where density reads as power.
rationale: About 2.5 dB louder, bought with real limiting: roughly 47% of the file,
worst-case -3.3 dB gain reduction, loudness range 2.9 -> 2.5 LU and
That transient cost is what makes it worse on small speakers and better
on a rig that can move air. Do not ship it as the only master.

louder_still: There is no profile above -9. --lufs -6 is reachable but limits roughly 90% of a typical set here; if anyone wants it, they should listen to it first.
how_to_judge: Level-match before comparing. Louder always flatters, so an unmatched A/B tells you nothing -- match both to the same LUFS and the only thing left is what the limiting did.
